{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --job-name=combine-d1-output
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=1
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --mem-per-cpu=250m
#   --time=5:00:00
#   --account=pschloss1
#   --partition=standard
#   --mail-user=tomkoset@umich.edu
#   --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
#   --output=%x-%j.out
#   --export=ALL

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  -c 1 \
  --time=5h \
  --queue=standard \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=250m has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available
# (or contend more), increasing risk of OOM or slowdown.

# NOTE: Slurm --account=pschloss1 has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: Slurm email notifications (--mail-user/--mail-type) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive job emails.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=combine-d1-output is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: Slurm output naming uses %x/%j; Flux has no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but log naming/organization may be degraded.
# Best-effort: fixed name plus Flux job id.
exec >"combine-d1-output-${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>&1

# Slurm --export=ALL: environment is typically inherited by the shell here.

mkdir -p logs/slurm/

bash code/bash/family_d1_cat_csv_files.sh
'
"
}
